items.t: Ping An stock gains a new AI governance test for investors
sum: Ping An Bank has formalized board-level oversight of artificial intelligence, adding a governance layer as automated tools expand across compliance and operational reviews. The policy was disclosed on September 30, 2026, and The Asian Banker reported the framework on October 9.

The board strategy committee will coordinate AI development and application management. The framework covers data security, algorithm risk, ethical review and accountability across the technology lifecycle.

The additional governance detail is that Ping An Bank said the policy implements guidance issued by China's National Financial Regulatory Administration in June. AI risks are incorporated into comprehensive risk management and classified by risk level, linking board responsibility to applications already used in control functions.

Ping An Bank's interim report recorded more than 450 large-model use cases by June and 140 operational-review agents across 55 scenarios. The applications include anti-money-laundering due diligence and account review.

For investors, the policy moves the question beyond adoption toward execution. Formal oversight may help contain data, model and accountability risks, but the policy alone does not establish a financial return from the deployments. The next test is whether Ping An converts broader AI use into measurable efficiency while preserving control quality.

Ping An stock traded at 6.07 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 15:35 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026. The latest relevant prior report cited 6.07 euros on Thursday, November 5, at 15:35 CET, so the new governance detail, rather than a price move, is the main change in this update.
Investors can follow the real-time quote of Ping An stock for subsequent trading updates.

Ping An stock weighs stronger operating profit against earnings drop
sum: Ping An Insurance (Group) Company of China reported mixed nine-month results for the period ended September 30, 2026. Operating profit attributable to shareholders increased 8.3 percent year on year to RMB125,905 million, while net profit attributable to shareholders fell 27.3 percent to RMB96,645 million.

The results, released on October 28 and carried by Vietnam Investment Review from a PR Newswire release, show the contrast between recurring operating performance and investment-sensitive reported earnings. Basic operating earnings per share rose 9.2 percent year on year to RMB7.23.

Life and health insurance operating profit rose 5.7 percent to RMB87,238 million. Ping An Property and Casualty's premium income increased 3.5 percent to RMB265,215 million, while its combined ratio improved by 1.4 percentage points year on year to 95.6 percent. A ratio below 100 percent indicates underwriting profitability before investment income.

Not all insurance indicators moved in the same direction. Life and health new business value declined 13.3 percent year on year to RMB30,987 million, highlighting pressure on the value of newly written business despite higher operating profit in the segment.

Ping An Bank delivered moderate growth during the period. Revenue rose 2.4 percent year on year to RMB103,100 million, while net profit increased 2.2 percent to RMB39,186 million. The bank reported a non-performing loan ratio of 1.05 percent and a provision coverage ratio of 214.75 percent at September 30.

Technology remained a central part of Ping An's operating strategy. Its Express Service provided AI-enabled inquiry, consultation and processing in 90 percent of business scenarios by the end of September. The service had handled more than 150 million user sessions and resolved 91 percent of customer requests end to end with AI.

The group also said average daily token consumption exceeded 330 billion in September, more than ten times the December 2025 level. Token output per compute unit increased 509 percent, while cost per token declined 81 percent, according to the release.

Ping An stock weighs 8.3% operating-profit gain against profit drop
sum: Ping An Insurance (Group) Company of China, Ltd. released its unaudited results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, on October 28. The company said operating profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company increased 8.3 percent year on year to RMB125,905 million. The results were carried by stronger underlying insurance performance and wider use of artificial intelligence across customer-facing operations, according to the company release published by PR Newswire.

The quality of the result was mixed. Net profit attributable to shareholders fell 27.3 percent to RMB96,645 million from RMB132,856 million a year earlier, while revenue declined 12.6 percent to RMB787,634 million. Ping An said operating profit is intended to reflect recurring performance more clearly by excluding short-term investment volatility and one-off items.

Life and health insurance operating profit rose 5.7 percent to RMB87,238 million. Ping An Property and Casualty improved its combined operating ratio to 95.6 percent from 97.0 percent, a 1.4 percentage-point improvement. Life and health new business value nevertheless declined 13.3 percent to RMB30,987 million, showing that growth in recurring profitability did not extend across every insurance indicator.

Ping An also highlighted progress under its Service Year 2026 initiative. Its Express Service supported AI-enabled inquiry, consultation and processing in 90 percent of business scenarios by September 30. The service had handled more than 150 million user sessions and resolved 91 percent of customer requests end to end with AI, serving approximately 97 million monthly online active customers.

AI service representatives handled about 1,484 million interactions during the nine-month period, equivalent to 82 percent of total customer-service volume. The company also reported an 80 percent AI code penetration rate among employees and said 95 percent of life insurance policies were underwritten within seconds. These measures point to an efficiency program with broad operational reach, although the reported earnings decline underlines the continuing sensitivity of the group to investment returns.

sum: Ping An is turning artificial intelligence into an operating tool across insurance, customer service and healthcare. Ping An's Express Service covered 90 percent of business scenarios by September 30 and resolved 91 percent of customer requests end to end with AI. The service had assisted customers more than 150 million times. Ninety-five percent of life insurance policies were underwritten within seconds.

The broader nine-month picture is mixed. Operating profit attributable to shareholders increased 8.3 percent year on year to RMB125,905 million, while life and health insurance operating profit rose 5.7 percent to RMB87,238 million. Reported net profit fell 27.3 percent to RMB96,645 million as market-driven investment effects weighed on earnings.

Ping An's property and casualty business generated RMB265,215 million in premium income, up 3.5 percent. Its combined ratio improved by 1.4 percentage points to 95.6 percent, indicating underwriting profitability before investment income. New business value in life and health insurance declined 13.3 percent to RMB30,987 million, highlighting pressure in a key growth measure.

Hang Seng dips 237 points as insurers, banks weigh, chip stocks extend rally
sum: Hong Kong stocks closed lower on Monday, weighed down by losses in insurers and banks following Beijing's new multibillion-yuan capital injection plan, while chip makers continue to rally.
The benchmark Hang Seng Index fell 237 points, or 0.93 percent, to 25,413 points, delivering a full-day market turnover of HK$209 billion.
Chip makers continued their rally, with Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor (1347) advancing 4.92 percent and Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (0981) rising 1.64 percent.

Tech heavyweights delivered mixed performances. Baidu (9888) and Xiaomi (1810) extended their losses, falling 4.69 percent and 3.31 percent, respectively. Xiaomi is set to unveil new foldable smartphones and other products this evening. Meituan (3690) slid 2 percent, while JD.com (9618) edged 1.45 percent lower. Tencent (0700) and Alibaba (9988) slipped 0.99 percent and 0.45 percent, respectively.
BYD Electronics surged 6.84 percent to top the blue-chip gainers, followed by Li Auto (2015), which rose 5.4 percent. In contrast, Geely Auto (0175) fell 2.84 percent.

Insurance and banking stocks came under pressure after five state-owned insurers and three banks announced plans to raise up to 360 billion yuan (HK$420.61 billion) through capital injections from the Ministry of Finance and other shareholders. Agricultural Bank of China (1398) and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (1288) dropped 2.45 percent and 2.47 percent, respectively.

Other Hong Kong-listed Chinese insurers and banks also took a hit. China Life (2628) declined 1.1 percent, while Ping An Insurance (2318) fell 1.57 percent. China Merchants Bank (3968), China Construction Bank (0939), and Bank of China (3988) dropped 2.72 percent, 2.31 percent, and 1.98 percent, respectively.

items.t: Ping An unveils AI solutions in healthcare, insurance, payments at WAIC 2026
sum: Ping An Insurance (Group) Company of China, Ltd. showcased AI innovations at WAIC 2026, targeting healthcare, insurance, and payments. Highlights include a disease-specific AI portfolio, 100% AI coverage in P&C operations, and a financial AI assistant for 251 million users. The moves reinforce its strategy to integrate finance with health and senior care services.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

Ping An Insurance (Group) Company of China, Ltd. unveiled a range of innovative artificial intelligence (AI) products and services at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference 2026 (WAIC 2026). Spanning healthcare, insurance, and payments scenarios, these innovations further advance the AI-driven development of Ping An's "integrated finance + health and senior care" strategy. The Group's initiatives aim to enhance service efficiency and customer experience across its ecosystems.

Ping An's latest healthcare AI applications focus on complex disease diagnosis, treatment, and everyday health management. The Group launched its first "disease-specific AI product portfolio" for patients with cancer and other critical illnesses. This portfolio includes disease prediction services, disease-specific insurance, and the Peking University Healthcare AI Disease Manager. These offerings connect disease risk identification, insurance protection, and professional healthcare services.

For everyday health management, the "AI Family Doctor" from Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited serves 90 million monthly active users. The service uses an "AI + Physician" model, where AI handles high-frequency needs such as consultation triage and medication reminders, while physicians manage complex conditions. Ping An's AI Doctor supports accurate diagnosis across more than 11,300 diseases and serves nearly 12 million users annually.

Ping An Property & Casualty has achieved 100% AI coverage across its core business scenarios, improving overall operational efficiency by 80%. AI now empowers the entire insurance value chain, including services, marketing, operations, and business management.
Ping An Bank Credit Card introduced an all-scenario AI credit card, allowing cardholders to redeem points for AI computing resources.

items.t: Webull Australia lets share traders earn Qantas Points through Frequent Flyer tie-up
sum: SYDNEY, July 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Webull Securities (Australia) Pty Ltd ("Webull Australia"), a subsidiary of Webull Corporation (NASDAQ: BULL), the owner of the Webull trading platform, today announced a new partnership with Qantas Frequent Flyer that will enable new and existing eligible clients to earn Qantas Points. This offer gives clients three ways to earn Qantas Points via Webull Australia, which include:

New clients who reach an eligible balance of AUD$2,000 or more will earn 1 Qantas Point per AUD$1, capped at 100,000 points. Offer available from 1 July 2026 to 30 September 2026. Points are awarded in four instalments when you retain your balance until 31 July 2027.

"We want to give investors another reason to choose Webull, and partnering with the largest national airline loyalty program in Australia, Qantas Frequent Flyer, helps us do just that," said Rob Talevski, CEO of Webull Australia. "In addition, rewarding our clients for building their portfolios and trading in global markets felt like a natural addition to our overall offering. This partnership gives clients a new and compelling way to keep earning Qantas Points through an activity they're already doing."

Webull is a CHESS-sponsored broker, and one of the few global share trading platforms to hold both ASX and Cboe Australia market participant status. The platform combines zero-brokerage investing across multiple markets, 24/5 access to US markets, and real-time market data, an AI powered assistant, and advanced investing tools to support clients at every stage of their journey.

Ping An Bank, UnionPay, and Tencent Launch China's First "AI Compute Card," Shifting Bank Card Rewards from Gift Points to LLM Compute Power
sum: Competition in bank card rewards is shifting from traditional point-based gift exchanges and airline miles toward the more tech-forward appeal of large language model (LLM) compute power. On June 30, Ping An Bank, together with China UnionPay and Tencent Cloud, officially launched China's first debit card designed for personal AI compute consumption—the "AI Compute Card." The product directly links users' daily payment behavior with AI productivity, signaling that financial institutions are beginning to participate deeply in the push to make AI accessible to the masses. The move aims to lock in younger customers and digital productivity workers through "compute-power rewards" in an era of fierce competition for market share.

According to a report by China Business News (CBN), the card integrates three core functions: aggregated compute-power payments, basic financial services, and exclusive compute-power rewards. Cardholders accumulate compute-power points according to set rules through card spending or by reaching certain asset tiers, creating an experience where "using the card accumulates compute power." Applications for the card will gradually open in July through Ping An Bank's Pocket Bank app and offline branches. Ping An Bank also plans to launch a credit card under the same theme in July, forming a product matrix that links debit and credit functions.

In this collaboration, the three parties have clearly defined roles, jointly building a closed loop from compute infrastructure to front-end applications. China UnionPay provides the cloud computing platform and an aggregated entry point for AI large language models. Tencent Cloud supplies AI office and learning tools centered on WorkBuddy. Ping An Bank is responsible for the account system, customer operations, and financial service integration.

UnionPay's cloud computing platform has completed the private deployment and aggregated access to multiple mainstream AI large language models, building a secure and controllable compute resource pool. Users no longer need to repeatedly register, top up, or switch between multiple AI platforms.

items.t: Merdeka Gold Debuts in Hong Kong in Indonesia’s First Dual Listing in Over 20 Years
sum: Jakarta. Merdeka Gold Resources (EMAS) began trading on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on Friday through a Hong Kong Depositary Receipts (HDR) listing, marking the first dual listing by an Indonesian company in Hong Kong in more than two decades.
The company's HDRs started trading at 9:30 a.m. Hong Kong time at an offer price of HK$26.60 per HDR, with each board lot consisting of 100 HDRs.

The listing represents a milestone both for Merdeka Gold Resources and Indonesia's capital market, becoming the first Indonesian issuer to secure a dual listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in over 20 years. It is also the first HDR listing in Hong Kong in more than a decade.
President Director Boyke Poerbaya Abidin said the secondary listing would broaden the company's access to international investors while raising its profile in global capital markets.
"The successful listing on HKEX marks an important milestone for Merdeka Gold Resources and strengthens Indonesia's presence in global capital markets," Boyke said on Friday.

"The transaction provides wider access for international investors to gain exposure to one of Indonesia's most significant gold growth assets and reflects confidence in the quality of the Pani Gold Project."
The company expects the dual listing to expand its investor base, improve global visibility, and support its next phase of growth.
